description: Self-authored (not sourced from any corpus, not written by PlumePdf's own writer) page with a raw (unrotated) MediaBox of 200x400 points and a page-level /Rotate 90 entry (ISO 32000-1 7.7.3.3: displayed clockwise-rotated by 90 degrees, so the visual page is 400x200 landscape). The content stream itself contains ordinary, non-rotated horizontal text in the page's raw coordinate space — this fixture is about /Rotate NORMALIZATION (extracted positions are in post-/Rotate page space), not about text painted at an arbitrary text-matrix rotation angle. Deliberately does not assert letter origins: correctly re-deriving the exact sign/offset convention of the raw-to-visual coordinate transform by hand (independent of PlumePdf's own implementation) risks encoding the same mistake this test exists to catch, so only text CONTENT is asserted — proving the reader neither crashes nor drops/garbles text under /Rotate is this fixture's value.

oracle.method: hand-derived: content stream is `BT /F1 16 Tf 20 350 Td (Rotated page sample) Tj ET`, unambiguous regardless of /Rotate handling since text content itself is not rotation-dependent.
oracle.notes: See 'description' for why letter-level positions are intentionally out of scope for this fixture.
